title: Dyadic prefix compression: primitive coordinates, block margins, and unsafe-skip barriers

concepts.label: odd-denominator residual transport
concepts.note: Subtracting a reduced odd-denominator prefix from a dyadic target preserves that entire odd denominator through rational reduction, up to a remaining power-of-two factor.

concepts.label: dyadic excess numerator
concepts.note: The division-free integer coordinate E=2^n p-L for a displayed residual p/(2L), with affine skip recurrence E(n+1)=2E(n)+L.

concepts.label: Mersenne-dyadic forbidden sliver
concepts.note: A skipped next rank is dyadically unsafe exactly in the finite integer window 0<E and 2E<p.

concepts.label: gcd-free successor-block margin
concepts.note: All skips between consecutive takes compress to one final-rank inequality, and common reduction factors cancel from the resulting raw margin.

concepts.label: two-channel cap
concepts.note: The dyadic channel plus the first 4-adic correction, whose comparison with the residual becomes one exact integer inequality.

concepts.label: primitive greedy prefix coordinates
concepts.note: The reduced numerator and odd denominator of the actual finite half-greedy prefix, related to raw support coordinates by the exact cancellation gcd.

concepts.label: unsafe Mersenne sandwich
concepts.note: The interval p(2^c-1)<2D<p2^c characterising a skipped but dyadically unsafe displayed residual.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED DENOMINATOR TRANSPORT: subtracting a reduced odd-denominator fraction from a dyadic fraction cannot cancel any odd factor of the denominator. For the actual finite half-greedy prefix, the prefix denominator is odd, the residual has an exact p/(2D) display, and finite support sums agree under the rational-to-real cast.
statement_nodes.engine: coprimality of powers of two with an odd denominator, exact rational reduction, and finite-support cast transport
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: General-purpose rational denominator algebra specialised to the binary Mersenne-prefix coordinates; the module expressly makes no novelty or priority claim.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Odd-part survival excludes cancellation and boundary ties, but it neither supplies infinitely many safe skips nor proves that one half belongs to the Mersenne achievement set.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED AFFINE SKIP DYNAMICS: for a displayed residual p/(2L) whose numerator and denominator do not change during a skip run, the dyadic excess satisfies E(n+1)=2E(n)+L and hence E(n+k)=2^k E(n)+(2^k-1)L. The rational distance from the next dyadic point is exactly E divided by 2^(n+1)L.
statement_nodes.engine: direct expansion of E=2^n p-L and induction on the skip length
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: An exact integer normal form for the module's rational greedy coordinate; no priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The recurrence describes a run after its take/skip pattern is fixed. It does not prove that the actual orbit has arbitrarily long, safe, or cofinal skip runs.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED EXACT DECISION CLASSIFIER: for p/(2L), E<=0 is exactly the safe side of the next dyadic boundary, 2E
statement_nodes.engine: positive-denominator cross multiplication and the identity decisionDefect=2E-p
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A lossless Diophantine encoding of the analytic greedy comparisons.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The classifier locates an unsafe skip if one occurs; it does not rule out unsafe skips in the actual half-greedy orbit.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED CAP GEOMETRY: comparison of p/(2L) with the next two-channel cap is exactly 3*2^(n+1)E<=L. On the actual half-greedy orbit, positivity of E detects landing above the dyadic boundary, 2E
statement_nodes.engine: exact rational display of the half-greedy residual followed by denominator clearing
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact arithmetic socket for a project-specific two-channel sufficient condition.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The equivalence does not prove the cap inequality at every skipped rank. That universal producer remains an open antecedent in the downstream membership theorem.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED BLOCK COMPRESSION: between a take at rank a and the next take at b, dyadic safety is monotone across the unchanged-residual skips. All intermediate skips are safe exactly when the block is adjacent or its final skip satisfies the single margin p*2^(b-1)<=2D; minimality alone yields only the strictly weaker predecessor bound p(2^(b-1)-1)<2D.
statement_nodes.engine: monotonicity of powers of two through a constant-residual skip block and exact first-take minimality
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A finite block normal form for the module's greedy arithmetic.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Compression reduces a block to one inequality; it does not prove that inequality for every actual successor block.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED GCD-FREE TRANSPORT: if the raw post-take coordinates (H,B) reduce by any positive common factor to the next displayed state, safety of every intervening skip is equivalent to the raw inequality H*2^(c-1)<=2B. Expanding H and B removes the gcd completely, adjacent takes inherit the margin automatically, and a gcd-scaled predecessor overshoot always implies the raw bound.
statement_nodes.engine: homogeneity of the block inequality under common-factor cancellation and elementary predecessor arithmetic
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A corrected cancellation-free formulation of the successor-block proof obligation.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem identifies the right primitive obligation and closes adjacent takes only. Nonadjacent successor blocks still require new orbit arithmetic.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED FORCED-BLOCK GEOMETRY: if a residual exceeds the two-channel cap at depth m>0, every one of the next 2m+2 Mersenne weights is greedily selected. Sharp higher-channel bounds place the remaining tails below explicit 8-adic and triple-depth thresholds, while exact subtraction shows that consecutive takes preserve signed distance from the full tail separatrix.
open_antecedents: a cap violation at a specified depth; the theorem describes its finite consequence and does not assert that such violations occur cofinally
statement_nodes.engine: finite greedy block selection plus geometric estimates for the channels of order at least three
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Project-specific exact tail estimates and their finite greedy consumer.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: A forced take block is not itself a contradiction: the residual and the true tail lose the same prefix. No cofinal safe-skip or achievement witness follows.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED EXACT CANCELLATION LAW: the common-to-reduced scale of the actual finite half-greedy prefix is precisely its numerator-denominator gcd. This same positive gcd multiplies both the raw residual numerator and the raw next-dyadic excess, so all sign and strict cap comparisons survive reduction; at a taken rank the new residual numerator satisfies a division-free recurrence with the exact take-step gcd.
statement_nodes.engine: normalisation of a rational common fraction and exact gcd cancellation in one take step
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Exact bridge between raw support-lattice coordinates and the primitive displayed greedy state.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: Cancellation invariance makes the finite tests honest; it supplies no inequality forcing all actual skipped ranks to be safe.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED ACTUAL-ORBIT RECURRENCES: a taken rank adds exactly its Mersenne unit fraction to the reduced prefix, while a skipped rank leaves that prefix and both displayed coordinates unchanged. Consequently the excess on a skip obeys E(n+1)=2E(n)+D with no hidden cancellation factor, and every displayed residual numerator remains nonnegative.
statement_nodes.engine: exact rational greedy recursion and the unchanged reduced fraction on skipped ranks
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Kernel-checked recurrence package for the actual half-greedy orbit.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The recurrences expose the finite state update but do not establish an asymptotic orbit invariant or infinitely many safe skips.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED FINITE FIXTURE SUPPORT: the second noninductivity example has denominator equal to the lcm of all Mersenne denominators through rank seven, and in the factor-eleven example ranks six through eight skip before rank nine becomes the first subsequent take. These exact facts support counterexamples showing that saturation or a strong predecessor margin does not propagate automatically.
statement_nodes.engine: kernel-normalised finite lcm arithmetic and exhaustive checking of three take/skip decisions
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Project-specific finite falsification fixtures; no asymptotic or priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The fixtures refute particular proposed inductive invariants only. They neither refute Erdős #257 nor establish behavior beyond the displayed finite states.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: PROVED UNSAFE-SKIP BARRIER: if p is odd and p(2^c-1)<2D<p2^c, then both gcd(D,2^c-1) and gcd(D,2^(c+1)-1) are strictly smaller than p. Therefore every putative dyadically unsafe skip in the actual half-greedy orbit forces consecutive Mersenne gcd deficits below the current displayed residual numerator.
statement_nodes.engine: both adjacent gcds divide nonzero combinations of the positive overshoot delta=2D-p(2^c-1), whose size is strictly below p by the unsafe sandwich and oddness
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: A project-specific consecutive-gcd obstruction extracted from the exact unsafe window. External prior-art review has not been completed, so this is not a novelty claim.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: This is a necessary consequence of an unsafe skip, not a contradiction: no theorem here supplies a lower bound forcing either adjacent gcd to reach p. It does not solve #257.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The exact affine excess coordinate is the integer quantity whose sign and comparison with p classify every next-rank decision.
The two-channel test refines the same excess coordinate by comparing the first positive dyadic excess with the explicit 4-adic correction.
During an intervening skip block the displayed fraction is constant and the affine excess is monotone, leaving only the last skip to check.
The reduced-state last-margin criterion is transported back to raw post-take coordinates by cancelling their common positive factor.
The exact cap violation supplies the strict mass inequality that forces selection of the next 2m+2 weights.
Odd-denominator survival identifies the primitive residual display, while the exact gcd measures the remaining raw-to-reduced scaling.
The actual half-greedy prefix instantiates the abstract common-factor cancellation used by the gcd-free successor-block theorem.
The gcd law explains taken-rank reduction, while the take/skip recurrences give the exact state evolution on both branches.
The finite examples show that denominator saturation and a strong current predecessor margin do not inductively supply the next nonadjacent raw margin.
The gcd-free margin states the sufficient raw inequality; its failure on a skipped rank yields the adjacent-gcd deficit necessary condition.
The forbidden-sliver inequalities are exactly the unsafe Mersenne sandwich used to bound both adjacent gcds.
